# blakstrip

> Three private, in-browser tools for the files you are about to send someone: a PDF redactor that erases content rather than covering it, a photo metadata stripper, and an image compressor. Everything runs locally, nothing is uploaded, and each one re-reads the finished file to prove the result before you download it.

blakstrip runs entirely in the browser. The PDF tool renders your document with pdf.js and rasterizes the pages you redact, so the underlying text and vectors on those pages are gone rather than sitting behind a black box; before export it audits what is hiding in the file (author metadata and timestamps, XMP, annotations, form-field values, embedded JavaScript, attachments, EXIF/GPS in embedded images, optional-content layers) and strips what it can. The metadata tool walks the container itself (JPEG marker segments, PNG chunks, WebP RIFF chunks) and removes identifying data losslessly, copying the image bitstream byte for byte so nothing is re-encoded. The compressor does the opposite: it decodes to raw pixels and re-encodes them through MozJPEG, libwebp, OxiPNG or AVIF, which makes the file smaller and leaves metadata nowhere to survive, and it shows both versions at full size so you can judge the artefacts yourself. The wasm codecs are inlined in the page rather than fetched, except AVIF's, which is large enough to be loaded on demand. Every tool re-inspects its own output and shows you exactly what is still recoverable, including anything it could not remove; AVIF is the one output format the engine cannot read back, and the page says so rather than reporting a check it did not run. A strict Content-Security-Policy (`connect-src 'none'`) blocks network egress from the page, with a matching response-header policy over the workers that parse your file, and the app works fully offline as a PWA.

## Tools

- [Redact a PDF](https://blakstrip.com/pdf-redact): Drop a PDF, draw boxes or search a term and redact every instance, then export a cleaned file. Audits hidden data on load and verifies the output before download.
- [Remove image metadata](https://blakstrip.com/media-strip): Drop a JPEG, PNG or WebP and see what it is carrying (GPS location, camera make and serial, timestamps, embedded thumbnails, editing history), then remove it without touching the image.
- [Compress an image](https://blakstrip.com/image-compress): Drop a JPEG, PNG or WebP and make it smaller. Three presets or your own quality, effort and dimension cap; output as JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF; both versions shown at full size to compare before you download.

## About

- [Home](https://blakstrip.com/): What blakstrip is, and why removing content is different from covering it.

## Notes

- All processing is client-side. No files are uploaded, and no analytics are collected.
- Redacted PDF pages are rasterized (their text becomes an image); untouched pages keep selectable text.
- Metadata removal is lossless: the pixels are untouched and only the container around them is rewritten. Compression is a separate tool, and it does re-encode.
- Known limits: EXIF inside a photo *embedded in a PDF* is detected but not stripped, layer (optional-content) PDFs are not fully cleaned on copied pages, and encrypted PDFs are refused. All three are surfaced to the user rather than hidden.
- Built by sixra.dev (https://sixra.dev)
